business_need_date.description: Documented business or clinical control date that the decision must protect (ISO date).

coverage_item_or_resource.description: Immutable item or resource whose requirement and eligible coverage were reconciled.

decision_timing_status.description: ON_TIME when the selected outcome is on or before the control date; otherwise LATE.

earliest_qualified_base_window.description: First non-displacing farm window on or after standard staging readiness (ISO date).

escalation_approval_required.description: Use 1 when an alternative is outside current authority and would need a separate approval; otherwise 0.

expedite_completion_days_saved.description: Days the expedited retrieval saves after the window calendar is reapplied.

expedited_external_readiness.description: Expedited readiness date independently confirmed for Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214.

external_recovery_quantity.description: Uncovered SEGMENT that the external recovery must cover.

observed_coverage_quantity.description: Gross observed coverage for restorable IMG-ATLAS-25 segments at the nearline store before exclusions.

outcome_vs_control_days.description: Selected outcome date minus the documented control date; positive means late.

quantity_unit.description: Unit shared by the requirement and coverage calculations: SEGMENT.

recommended_incremental_cost_usd.description: Documented incremental cost of the selected option in USD; zero when spend is not a decision driver.

recommended_option.description: Best authorized option identifier after comparing standard_retrieval_plan, expedite_vendor_retrieval, rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours.

recommended_outcome_date.description: Date produced by the selected option after applying every source constraint (ISO date).

required_payload_gb.description: Payload per bundle taken from the current final metering, not a stale one.

required_quantity.description: 25 GB archive segments required to stage the 26.1 release and 26.0 rollback bundles at the current 118 GB bundle metering

segments_per_unit.description: Whole archive segments per bundle after the fixed-segment rounding rule.

selected_runner_window.description: Runner and window used by the selected option, as RUNNER/YYYY-MM-DD/SESSION.

shortage_quantity.description: Uncovered SEGMENT after netting eligible coverage from the requirement.

standard_external_readiness.description: Standard readiness date independently confirmed for Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214.

units_in_scope.description: Bundles the rollback-gate rule requires staged before the train is scheduled.

usable_coverage_quantity.description: Net eligible coverage after removing checksum-failed and purge-queued IMG-ATLAS-25 segments.

decision_model.binding_constraint: staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar; checksum-failed and purge-queued IMG-ATLAS-25 segments = 5 SEGMENT; uncovered scope = 3 SEGMENT

calculations.description: Preserved 2026-04-23 as the documented control date for the Atlas 26.1 release and rollback staging; did not infer urgency from a title or a request tone.
Derived 10 SEGMENT for 25 GB archive segments required to stage the 26.1 release and 26.0 rollback bundles at the current 118 GB bundle metering at revision v1.
Read 12 SEGMENT of gross observed restorable IMG-ATLAS-25 segments at the nearline store.
Excluded 5 SEGMENT for checksum-failed and purge-queued IMG-ATLAS-25 segments.
Calculated 12 observed − 5 ineligible = 7 usable SEGMENT.
Calculated 10 required − 7 usable = 3 SEGMENT uncovered.
Kept every planning quantity in SEGMENT.
Calculated standard_retrieval_plan outcome as 2026-04-22 under regular farm windows that do not displace protected release-freeze or compliance blocks.
Calculated expedite_vendor_retrieval outcome as 2026-04-22 using Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214.
Calculated rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours outcome as 2026-04-21 and kept its separate-approval condition.
Read 2026-04-22 as the independently confirmed standard readiness date for Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214.
Read 2026-04-20 as the independently confirmed expedited readiness date for Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214.
Bound external recovery to the 3 SEGMENT uncovered requirement rather than ordering the full header quantity.
Used the 2026-04-10 metering of 118 GB per bundle; did not use the stale January metering of 92 GB.
Kept the metered payload in GB.
Rounded 118 GB up to 5 immutable 25 GB segments under the whole-segment rule.
Applied the rollback-gate rule: both the 26.1 release bundle and the 26.0 rollback baseline must be staged before the train, so 2 bundles are in scope.
Identified 2026-04-22 (RUNNER-2 PM) as the first free window on or after the 2026-04-22 standard readiness that displaces no protected block.
Bound the verification run to RUNNER-2/2026-04-22/PM, the exact window that was free.
Compared the 2026-04-20 expedited readiness with the window calendar and proved the first free window is still 2026-04-22, so expediting saves 0 days.
Applied USD 0 as the documented incremental cost for standard_retrieval_plan; did not invent a premium where spend is not a decision driver.
Recognized that rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours remains outside current authority and requires an additional approval.

Compared the timing, cost, control status, and consequence of standard_retrieval_plan, expedite_vendor_retrieval, rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours; selected standard_retrieval_plan because it alone gives the best currently authorized result under staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar.
Calculated 2026-04-22 as the supported outcome date for standard_retrieval_plan.
Compared 2026-04-22 with the independent control date 2026-04-23 and calculated a signed variance of -1 day(s).
Reported ON_TIME; did not relabel a controlled but late result as on time.

facts.rubric: Located IMG-ATLAS-25 using immutable identifiers and preserved effective revision v1: service code atlas-core resolves to SVC-20411 and open ticket RT-51203; the similarly named atlas-core-legacy (RT-51188, closed) is a different service.
facts.statement: HOST-0001: service code atlas-core resolves to SVC-20411 and open ticket RT-51203; the similarly named atlas-core-legacy (RT-51188, closed) is a different service; the effective revision is v1.

facts.rubric: Applied the effective ticket and runbook to establish 10 SEGMENT for 25 GB archive segments required to stage the 26.1 release and 26.0 rollback bundles at the current 118 GB bundle metering, with control date 2026-04-23.
facts.statement: The effective ticket and runbook establish 25 GB archive segments required to stage the 26.1 release and 26.0 rollback bundles at the current 118 GB bundle metering = 10 SEGMENT: the ticket is metered at the 2026-04-10 bundle size of 118 GB (5 segments per bundle) and the rollback-gate rule keeps both bundles staged, so 10 segments are required. The control date is 2026-04-23 (the 26.1 release train departs at 09:00 on 2026-04-23; staging and verification must be complete before it).

facts.rubric: Reconciled 12 observed less 5 excluded to 7 supported SEGMENT for restorable IMG-ATLAS-25 segments at the nearline store.
facts.statement: the holdings workbook shows 12 IMG-ATLAS-25 segments in gross; the register fails 9077 (2 segments) on the scrub and 9084 (3 segments) sits inside the purge-queue horizon, so 7 segments are restorable; eligibility requires netting the exclusions rather than trusting a header total.

facts.rubric: Used the independently confirmed 2026-04-20 expedited readiness input for expedite_vendor_retrieval, then separately derived its 2026-04-22 operating outcome under staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar instead of treating a vendor promise as authorization or a completion date.
facts.statement: Coldspur's confirmed standard and expedited retrieval dates on RQ-88214: Coldspur RQ-88214 confirms standard retrieval 2026-04-21 and expedited 2026-04-17 (+USD 240); staging release is the next business day after checksum verification; a vendor confirmation alone proves neither eligibility nor approval.

facts.rubric: Applied regular farm windows that do not displace protected release-freeze or compliance blocks to derive the three option outcomes without using protected or blocked windows.
facts.statement: regular farm windows that do not displace protected release-freeze or compliance blocks: the window calendar's first free window on or after 2026-04-22 is RUNNER-2 PM on 2026-04-22; RUNNER-1 AM on 2026-04-20 is the protected freeze verification and cannot be displaced; protected and blocked windows cannot be displaced.

facts.rubric: Applied AP-HO-0101 only to standard_retrieval_plan and IMG-ATLAS-25; kept rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours outside current authority.
facts.statement: AP-HO-0101 covers one Coldspur retrieval up to 6 segments with an expedite fee up to USD 250; out-of-hours runner blocks need the SRE lead. The approval does not select an option in advance and does not authorize rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours.

facts.rubric: Compared all three alternatives and selected standard_retrieval_plan: it is the best currently authorized response that satisfies staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar.
facts.statement: the release meeting needs one defensible verification date before the 2026-04-23 train; a faster or broader action has value only if it remains inside staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar.

options.consequence: standard retrieval plan stages only verified restorable segments plus the standard Coldspur pull, lands on the first non-displacing verification window on 2026-04-22, one day before the train, at no incremental cost.
options.label: standard_retrieval_plan: outcome 2026-04-22, incremental cost USD 0, SUPPORTED_AND_APPROVED

options.consequence: expedite vendor retrieval would have segments verified into staging by 2026-04-20 and adds USD 240, but the first non-displacing verification window is still 2026-04-22, so it saves 0 days.
options.label: expedite_vendor_retrieval: outcome 2026-04-22, incremental cost USD 240, FEASIBLE_WITH_INFERIOR_TRADEOFF

options.consequence: rebuild from source out of hours would finish 1 day earlier than standard retrieval plan and adds USD 620 of overtime staffing, but out-of-hours runner blocks need the SRE lead's separate approval, which AP-HO-0101 does not carry.
options.label: rebuild_from_source_out_of_hours: outcome 2026-04-21, incremental cost USD 620, SEPARATE_APPROVAL_OR_POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED

decision_model.recommendation_reason: standard_retrieval_plan is the best currently authorized response that satisfies staging readiness versus the non-displacing farm window calendar and lands 1 day(s) on or before the control date.

instruction: Last night's Atlas publish died halfway through and the 26.1 train is supposed to leave Thursday morning. Before the release meeting I need the honest picture: how many archive segments the release and its rollback baseline actually need at the current bundle size, how many of what the catalog shows are genuinely restorable once the scrub failures and the purge queue are set aside, whether Coldspur's retrieval changes the date, and what a from-source rebuild would really involve. Book the verification window that works and leave Freya a draft she can take into the meeting. Anything that needs Annika or Bisi should be flagged, not assumed.
